newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to monitor Australia's anthrax outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to monitor Australia's anthrax outbreak.

text.p: Hong Kong's health authority is closely monitoring the outbreak of the disease anthrax in dairy herds in Australia, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The Health Department will liaise with the Australian trade commission for further information on the incident and further monitor developments," the spokesman said by telephone.

The disease, a bacterial infection which causes quick death among cattle, sheep and goats when they eat contaminated soil or feed, was discovered in at least 31 dairy heards in Goulburn Valley in Victoria state in the last couple of days.
But the Hong Kong government also sought to reassure that imported beef from Australia was safe for consumption.

"All imported meat from Australia is required to be accompanied by an official health certificate issued by the health authority in Australia," the spokesman said, adding that thorough cooking at 100 degrees Celsius can kill anthrax.
